title: MonsterNums
summary: A math-learning platform for kids with ADHD. I joined as UX writer and content strategist, then co-led design of its onboarding, customization and design system.
tagline: Math for neurodivergent learners. UX writer turned design co-lead.
intro: MonsterNums, first called Mindful Digits, is a math-learning platform for 8- to 11-year-olds with ADHD and other neurodivergences, built in phases by teams at Tech Fleet. I joined as a UX writer and content strategist, then came back for the next phase as UX design co-lead.
role: UX Writer, then UX Design Co-Lead
body:
## Key objectives

- Engage kids in lessons with simple, concise, friendly language.
- Let each learner customize the experience to fit their needs.
- Give the product a consistent, accessible visual system.

![Project timeline: UX writing, customization, design system](/images/monsternums/mn-timeline.webp)

*The project in three stages: UX writing, customization, then the design system.*

## Phase 1: Finding the voice

Our content team joined in sprint 4 of 8, so we worked from the existing research and our own secondary research on math curriculum for children with ADHD, then refined the copy as usability results came in.

We wrote content guidelines built on three principles: educate, empower and respect. For the brand personality we pictured teachers who love their subject, like Bill Nye, Steve Irwin and Alton Brown. We avoided humor, which wasn’t developmentally right for young learners already struggling with math at school.

![Content guidelines](/images/mindful-digits/content-guidelines.png)

*Voice qualities and tone from the content guidelines.*

Then we rewrote the app’s copy. On the dashboard, “Training Grounds” and “Today’s Adventure” replaced labels that felt like a typical classroom, to suggest growth and a journey.

![Dashboard copy before and after](/images/monsternums/mn-copy-dashboard.webp)

*Dashboard copy, before and after.*

In lessons, we used simple, direct language and made font weight and color carry the focus.

![Lesson copy before and after](/images/monsternums/mn-copy-lesson.webp)

*Lesson copy, before and after.*

Usability participants weren’t sure what reflection words like “Hopeful” meant, so each now has a short description.

![Reflection copy before and after](/images/monsternums/mn-copy-reflection.webp)

*Reflection choices, before and after.*

The original name, All Minds Math, turned out to be taken. Our team led the renaming: open brainstorming sessions, a shortlist of five, and a vote across all teams. Mindful Digits won with 20 votes.

![Voting for the new name](/images/mindful-digits/2-voting-for-name.png)

*The vote for the new name.*

## Phase 2: Co-leading design

In the next phase I co-led a six-person design team and mentored five apprentice designers. Customization was the product’s core idea, so we started there: from 58 ideas, we chose 7 to launch with, including background noise, breaks, closed captions, font types and color themes.

![Map of customization options, with the first ones to build](/images/monsternums/mn-customization.webp)

*The full map of customization ideas, and the first ones we built.*

I redesigned onboarding so that customization starts on the first screen, with separate flows for the adult setting up the account and for the learner. A friendly math buddy walks kids through each step.

![Onboarding step where the math buddy explains how to change the way things look](/images/monsternums/mn-onboarding.webp)

*Onboarding: the math buddy introduces customization.*

We then built an ADHD-friendly design system, starting from the existing Mindful Digits palette and log-in screen.

![The starting palette and log-in screen](/images/monsternums/mn-design-system-start.webp)

*The starting point.*

We explored three color directions, warm yellows that evoke paper, blue and green, and monochromatic blues, and gathered feedback from the whole team on each. Blue and green was the favorite.

![Four log-in explorations with team feedback notes](/images/monsternums/mn-explorations.webp)

*Color explorations, with the team’s feedback.*

The final components use Atkinson Hyperlegible for type: buttons in every state, read-aloud audio buttons, a progress stepper and dialogue boxes for the math buddy.

![Component library: buttons, audio buttons, stepper and dialogue boxes](/images/monsternums/mn-components.webp)

*The component library.*

## Outcome

Across both phases, MonsterNums gained a voice, a name, an onboarding flow built around customization, and an accessible design system for the next team to build on.
